currentAssessment.verdict: The Gironde fire is now described as contained but still not fixed, with Tuesday heat reactivation risk; Cap Ferret access and no-return instructions remain unchanged.
currentAssessment.narrative: The newest reviewed material signal is Le Monde’s 19:47 CEST live-index update during the presidential visit, citing the Gironde SDIS director: reprises de feu occurred during the day, a reactivation is feared Tuesday as temperatures rise, and the fire is contained but not fixed. This refines the earlier 19:00 smoke-and-response synthesis without creating a return signal. Atmo Nouvelle-Aquitaine still reports bad, very bad and extremely bad air-quality indices across much of Gironde, Landes and Lot-et-Garonne from an active PM10 episode caused by Gironde/Landes fire smoke. Bordeaux Airport’s board remains active, but its hotel-zone evacuation and tram disruption remain separate ground-access constraints. Inforoutes still warns against travel to Saumos, Le Porge, Lège-Cap-Ferret, Arès, Andernos-les-Bains and Marcheprime. For Cap Ferret, the practical conclusion is unchanged: the peninsula remains evacuated, inbound public access is unavailable, road reopening and essential commerce have not been confirmed, and there is no tourist reopening signal.
currentAssessment.confidence: High confidence that the fire-control signal has improved only to contained/not fixed because Le Monde attributes the newest entry to the Gironde SDIS director, while the Gironde prefecture’s 14:00 CEST point still described the situation as unfavorable and AP separately reports the fire has stopped growing but remains a threat before renewed heat. High confidence that smoke and air-quality risk remains material because Atmo Nouvelle-Aquitaine directly attributes bad to extremely bad regional indices and an active PM10 episode to Gironde/Landes fire smoke. High confidence that the Cap Ferret practical reopening signal remains negative because evacuation and no-return instructions have not been lifted, Inforoutes continues to warn against travel to affected sectors, and the mayor’s no-return-until-mastery signal remains operative.
priorities: Newest material update: Le Monde’s 19:47 CEST live-index entry cites the Gironde SDIS director saying the fire is contained but still not fixed, with reactivation feared Tuesday as temperatures rise.
The control-status signal is better than uncontrolled spread but still not a return trigger: not fixed, reprises de feu occurred during the day, and heat risk is increasing.
Smoke remains a material health context: Atmo Nouvelle-Aquitaine reports bad to extremely bad air-quality indices and an active PM10 episode from Gironde/Landes fire smoke.
Cap Ferret-specific decision driver: the Lège-Cap-Ferret mayor says no one should return until the fire is mastered.
The broader official baseline remains severe: the Gironde prefecture reports 42,000 hectares burned and about 220,000 preventive evacuations in 23 communes.
Regional access remains directly relevant: A63 and departmental road closures, repeated evacuation moves and transport disruption affect the wider approach to the Bassin.
Bordeaux Airport remains operational on its flight board, but hotel-zone evacuation and tram-stop disruption remain separate ground-access constraints.
Cap Ferret practical status remains negative: the peninsula is evacuated, public inbound access is unavailable and no normal tourist reopening has been announced.

La Depeche’s 18:09 live summary reports the A400M made its first retardant drop near Lacanau around 17:00, while the prefect described the threat as still very serious, with 1,400 firefighters mobilised and 140 houses destroyed in Gironde. The direct Gironde prefecture total remains 167,000 preventive evacuations and nearly 32,700 hectares burned at noon; AP still supports the wider Gironde/Landes evacuation context of about 197,000 people.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: This converts the earlier A400M planning signal into an active response-resource update and raises the reported property-damage toll from the previous roughly 100/109-house range to 140 houses in Gironde. It does not change the decision layer for Cap Ferret: the peninsula remains evacuated, inbound public access is unavailable, and Bordeaux Airport operation remains separate from disrupted ground access.

materialUpdates.title: Wind reversal turns the fire toward metropolitan Bordeaux; further evacuations are being prepared
materialUpdates.detail: Reuters reports that the uncontrolled Gironde fire changed orientation late Friday after a wind reversal and began progressing east toward the Bordeaux metropolitan area. The interior minister described the phenomenon as unprecedented and reported about 14,000 hectares burned and more than 110,000 Gironde evacuations. Franceinfo reports preparations for three additional metropolitan evacuations, says residents of Saint-Médard-en-Jalles and Saint-Jean-d’Illac should be ready for a probable evacuation, and records severe outbound congestion at Andernos. A later media report places the affected area near 19,000 hectares; that higher figure awaits matching official confirmation.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: This is a new trajectory and evacuation phase: the fire is no longer advancing only around the northern Bassin and peninsula corridor but has turned east toward metropolitan Bordeaux. The strongest late totals rise from 12,500 to about 14,000 hectares and from 44,000 to more than 110,000 Gironde evacuations, with a later media estimate near 19,000 hectares.

access.name: Travel to the peninsula
access.detail: The entire peninsula remains under an evacuation order. Public inbound travel is not permitted; Lège-Cap-Ferret town hall still says not to return, road access is closed and the partial Arcachon Bay reopening does not create a public maritime route to Cap Ferret.

access.name: Road access · Cap Ferret
access.detail: No authority has announced that ordinary inbound road access to Cap Ferret village or Bélisaire has reopened. The evacuation order and peninsula access restrictions still apply.

access.name: Maritime leisure activities
access.detail: Some Arcachon Bay zones far from the fire have reopened, but the peninsula remains evacuated and the maritime-prefecture order keeps the west-coast corridor and embarkation-point safety zones closed.

access.name: Beaches
access.detail: Residents and visitors have been told to leave the area. Municipal lifeguard stations are closed.

access.name: Cycling & hiking
access.detail: All forest cycle paths are closed; Gironde remains at red-level wildfire risk.

localCommerce.name: Groceries and food shops
localCommerce.detail: The evacuation order prevents normal customer access. No general reopening of supermarkets, food shops or the Cap Ferret market has been announced.

localCommerce.name: Pharmacies
localCommerce.detail: No pharmacy-specific reopening or public-access arrangement has been found. Emergency and authority instructions take priority over normal listed hours.

localCommerce.name: Other local shops and services
localCommerce.detail: There is no general announcement that visitor-facing retail or everyday local services have resumed.

ferries.name: Arcachon ↔ Bélisaire ferry
ferries.detail: Arcachon Bay has partly reopened away from the fire, but the west side of the bay and safety circles around Bélisaire, La Vigne, Le Canon, Grand Piquey and Piquey remain restricted. The UBA timetable is not an available public route to the evacuated peninsula.

ferries.name: Emergency evacuation shuttles
ferries.detail: The maritime-prefecture notice says the Union des Bateliers Arcachonnais evacuation boats have been suspended by decision of the Gironde prefect, while embarkation zones are preserved in case maritime evacuation resumes.

ferries.name: Excursions and leisure boats
ferries.status: Partly reopened away from the fire
ferries.detail: Sea users may return only to zones farthest from the fire. Navigation remains prohibited along the west-coast corridor of Arcachon Bay and within safety circles around the evacuation embarkation points.

overall.sourceName: Bordeaux Airport board updated at 21:07 CEST; prefectural evacuation notices

closure.status: Elevated risk · flights operating but heavily disrupted
closure.detail: The official board still lists arrivals and departures, but it flags 6 delayed and 2 cancelled arrivals, plus 0 delayed and 0 cancelled departures. The airport's own flash notice says activity continues, while the hotel zone around the airport is evacuated until further notice and the halls close overnight, so the site cannot provide accommodation. Treat flight operation, terminal overnight access and ground access as separate signals.

groundAccess.status: Disrupted · hotel zone evacuated and airport tram stops skipped
groundAccess.detail: Bordeaux Airport says activity continues and bus/tram services remain provided, but the tram is not stopping between Merignac Soleil and the airport. A separate airport flash notice says the surrounding hotel zone is evacuated by prefectural decision until further notice; because Hall A, Hall B and terminal billi are closed overnight, no accommodation can be provided on the airport site. Travellers are directed to hotels outside evacuated zones or the Parc des Expositions.
